# RECOIL Engine Source-Faithful Reimplementation Plan

## Purpose

This file is the source-cluster work breakdown for rebuilding Recoil as source-faithful native C/C++. Function addresses remain the stable evidence keys, but classes, provider boundaries, initialized-data groups, and subsystems are the implementation and validation units.

## End Goal

Use the currently loaded `Recoil.bndb` and `support/Recoil.exe` as the source of truth for behavior, ABI, layout, imports, and original assembly. Tier `C` functional coverage is the baseline; tier `B` additionally requires accepted `Source owner` and `Data reimplemented` evidence. Tier `S` is the tier `B` plus VC5SP3 byte/provider-ABI verification marker. Source-shape state is tracked separately by nested `Model:` metadata, so a function can be source-faithful without being tier `S`, and tier `S` does not by itself prove `Model: source-faithful`. ABI/source-shape scaffolds are not reimplementations; a function or source group that requires one must stay `Reimplemented [X]`/`❌` until proper source-faithful code replaces it.

## Plan Usage Rules

- Use `python tools/recoil.py plan next --lane binary` to select the next source-owner/tier `B`/tier `S` binary-lane blocker in dependency group order.
- Use `python tools/recoil.py plan group <id-or-name>` to inspect a class, source cluster, provider boundary, or subsystem.
- Authored entries track `Reconstructed`, `Source dependencies satisfied`, `Source owner`, `Data reimplemented`, and one tiered `Reimplemented [X/F/C/B/A/S]` marker. Provider entries track `Reconstructed` and `Provider-boundary`.
- The `Reimplemented` marker carries implementation metadata in nested detail bullets. Use `Reimplemented [S]` for byte/provider-ABI evidence, `Source owner` for standalone/class/structure/source-cluster ownership, and `Model:` for source-shape state; do not add separate source-pass metadata lines.
- `Source owner` is the standalone authored owner gate. `[❌]` means owner membership is not audited or the known parent owner remains pending. `[✅]` means current evidence proves the function is standalone or that the named parent class/structure/table/source cluster/subsystem was reconstructed source-faithfully for this function's contract.
- `Data reimplemented` is the standalone authored data gate. `[❌]` means touched-global data is not accepted, not audited, contradicted, or not yet source-faithful/binary-equivalent. `[❎]` means current evidence proves the entry or source group touches no authored globals. `[✅]` means every touched authored global is source-faithful and binary-equivalent against original `.data`, `.rdata`, or BSS evidence.
- `Target` is the functional verification target id for tier `C` or better. Any `Reimplemented` tier also requires that authored runtime-state access uses no raw-offset substitute and that authored callers do not depend on unsupported reconstruction helpers. Address-backed functions, accepted provider boundaries, and recovered original inlined/static/member helpers with documented caller evidence are valid source dependencies. Class/subsystem tier `S` evidence should use VC5SP3 verification across the smallest coherent source group.
- `Model: source-faithful` is the only accepted source-faithful source-shape marker. It requires `Source owner [✅]` and recreating the proven higher-order source owner when current evidence shows an authored class, interface, custom table object, source-file cluster, or method cluster; flattened isolated functions, raw table/slot scaffolds, or copied table arrays cannot claim source-faithfulness for code that originally belonged to such an owner. `Model: data-equivalent-only` and `Model: byte-equivalent-only` preserve accepted evidence without claiming source-faithfulness. `Model: abi-forced-scaffold` is legacy-invalid metadata: source-confirmed scaffold use requires downgrading `Reimplemented` to `❌`.
- Production source must use likely original VC5-era calling-convention and inline spelling. Do not use `RECOIL_*CALL`, reconstruction inline marker macros, noinline wrapper macros, or explicit `__thiscall`; member ABI must come from real C++ member syntax or a proven original custom-table/provider-header model. Forced thiscall, forced inline, noinline, provider-shim, or slot/table scaffolding cannot support any `Reimplemented` tier.
- Raw offsets in authored runtime-state access invalidate the affected entry or source cluster as a reimplementation, even when behavior evidence exists. Raw offsets include hard-coded object/member/layout offsets, named `...Offset` constants, manual object-relative byte/word pointer arithmetic, and offset-based loads or stores used instead of typed fields, structs, classes, provider types, or typed tables. `RECOIL_STATIC_ASSERT(offsetof(...))`, serialized/file-format offsets, PE/RVA/tooling facts, and evidence comments remain acceptable when they are not used to access reconstructed authored runtime state.
- Calls to unsupported reconstruction helpers invalidate the affected authored caller or source cluster as a reimplementation, even when behavior evidence exists. This includes reconstruction-only table builders, `Make...Vtable`/`Make...FTable` factories, provider stand-ins, provider ABI shims, member-address adapters, and similar scaffold helpers until replaced by the original source construct, real provider headers/types, or recovered original inline/static/member helper.
- `Data reimplemented [✅]` requires accepted `Source owner`, source-faithful binary-equivalent touched global shape and values, and is not valid when a global initializer calls or depends on an unsupported reconstruction helper. Leave the marker `[❌]` until the original initializer/source construct or recovered original helper is accepted.

## Group Catalog

Groups are dependency ordered. Provider/import groups come first, then engine foundations, engine runtime subsystems, Battlesport gameplay, UI/menu systems, and finally the Recoil application shell.
